title: add-rag-authoring-playbook-browser-runner
author: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Add a lightweight browser-based runner and Cypress E2E harness to the RAG Authoring Playbook quickstart. Motivation: customers frequently ask for a reproducible way to exercise authoring flows (index -> query -> tool calls -> edit) in a real browser to validate UX and telemetry. This PR introduces a small headless Chrome runner, Cypress scenarios that simulate tool-calling and snippet edits, and a recorder that emits trace snapshots compatible with the local-playback test harness.

What this includes: - A new docs page (quickstarts/browser-runner/README.md) that documents how to start the local mini-index, run the playbook in a devcontainer, and execute the E2E runner. - Cypress test suite with 3 scenarios: initial indexing smoke, conversational tool-call path, and incremental-authoring replay. The tests exercise streaming responses, structured output assertions, and trace exports. - A tiny Node utility (scripts/browser-runner.js) that bootstraps a headless session for CI and records a compressed trace (jsonl) for local replays. - Devcontainer improvements: forward ports, example env file, and a one-command start script that wires the local index and the playbook server. - CI integration: a github workflow quickstarts-e2e.yml that runs the runner in a matrix (node 18, 20) and publishes traces as artifacts.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: linked in PR description (ENG-1824) - [x] Local run instructions in README - [x] Cypress tests included and green in CI - [x] Telemetry export conforms to replay format - [x] Added smoke-level assertions to avoid brittle tests

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes. The browser runner and tests are opt-in for local development and CI.

How to validate locally: 1) Start the devcontainer or run `./scripts/start-local.sh` which spins up a compressed in-memory index and the authoring server. 2) Run `npm ci && npx cypress open` to debug or `npm run e2e:headless` to run the headless suite. 3) Review generated trace artifact at ./tmp/traces/latest.jsonl and replay with `./scripts/replay-trace.js`.

Notes: Kept test surface intentionally small to avoid long CI times (3–4 minutes per matrix cell). We plan future tests that exercise larger indexes behind a feature flag.
